stories.title: Zelenskyy meets US envoy in Oslo as Trump turns up the pressure
stories.body: President Zelenskyy met US envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders in Oslo, Norway, saying Ukraine has clear ideas on how to reach peace. Witkoff was due in Russia the next day. In Washington, President Trump said Zelenskyy has to want to settle the war, or it will be a very bad thing. Trump has also waived new sanctions on Russian oil and allowed Russian diesel exports, which Zelenskyy called a reward for President Putin.
stories.why: A deal, or a collapse of talks, would move world grain and fuel prices that feed Nigerian inflation.

cards.front: Where did Zelenskyy meet US envoy Steve Witkoff and European leaders on 20 October 2026?

stories.title: Qatar: the energy shock from the Iran war has not peaked
stories.body: Qatar's defence minister, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, told the Global Security Forum in Doha that the world has not yet felt the worst of the war's effect on energy. Iranian strikes in March damaged Qatar's Ras Laffan gas complex, and repairs will take several years. He rejected any transit fees for ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar, Pakistan and Oman are mediating between the US and Iran.
stories.why: Qatar is one of the world's biggest gas exporters, so damage there keeps global energy prices high for importers and raises the value of Nigeria's own gas.

cards.front: Which Qatari gas complex was damaged by Iranian strikes in March 2026?
cards.back: Ras Laffan; repairs are expected to take several years.

stories.title: AES and ECOWAS hold first talks since the split
stories.body: Ministers from ECOWAS and the Alliance of Sahel States (Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger) met in Dakar, Senegal, on 17 October. ECOWAS was led by Senegal's Foreign Minister Cheikh Niang and the AES by Burkina Faso's Foreign Minister Karamoko Jean-Marie Traoré. They agreed to set up joint working groups to draft a cooperation framework based on good neighbourliness and respect for sovereignty. The talks are about cooperation, not about the three states rejoining, and no timeline or trade deal was announced.
stories.why: Nigeria shares a long border with Niger, so any security and trade cooperation with the AES directly affects the North-west and North-east.

cards.front: Where did ECOWAS and the AES hold ministerial talks in October 2026?
What did ECOWAS and the AES agree in Dakar in October 2026?
cards.back: To set up joint working groups to draft a cooperation framework. Rejoining ECOWAS was not agreed.

stories.title: Hormuz attacks hit a record as oil reaches $110
stories.body: October has seen more attacks on ships than any month since the war began on 28 February. UK Maritime Trade Operations confirmed at least 12 ships attacked in the week to 16 October, and one, the GFS Pride, sank. The US and Iran both claim to control the Strait. Brent crude reached $110 a barrel, its highest since May. Pakistan and Qatar are still passing messages, but no breakthrough is expected before the 3 November US midterms.
stories.why: Higher oil prices raise Nigeria's export earnings but also the cost of imported fuel, shipping and food.

cards.front: What price did Brent crude reach in mid-October 2026?
cards.back: $110 a barrel, its highest since May 2026.

stories.title: Bandits tax and attack villages in Niger State
stories.body: Suspected bandits killed five farmers and abducted 18 people in attacks on Fanga (Mashegu LGA) and on Kigbere and Kokani (Borgu LGA) between 9 and 12 October. Residents of Fanga said the gang had imposed levies five times and attacked again when the community could not pay. Villagers in Rukukuje, Rijau LGA, fled after reports that bandits were moving in from Zamfara.
stories.why: Bandits charging illegal levies show they are acting like a parallel government in parts of the North-central and North-west.

cards.front: What is a bandit 'levy' in Nigeria's North-west and North-central?
cards.back: Money bandit gangs force communities to pay, under threat of attack.
